quests.instruction: Write b and d one after the other. Say which way each bump faces as you write.
quests.question: b d
quests.hint: b: stem first, bump on the right. d: circle first, then a stem on the right. The bump of b is after the stem, the bump of d is before it.
quests.explanation: b and d are mirror images, which makes them easy to swap. Checking the direction of the bump each time is the way to get them right.
quests.funFact: In most fonts the letters b and d are mirror images of each other, which is why they get mixed up so often.

quests.instruction: Write d, b, b in that order. Check each bump before you move on.
quests.question: d b b
quests.hint: Start with the d circle, then write two b's with the stem first and the bump on its right.
quests.explanation: A pattern of one letter followed by another makes you switch your hand from circle-first to stem-first.
quests.funFact: Words made from the same letters in a different order are called anagrams; 'bad' and 'dab' are an example.

quests.instruction: Write b, d, p and q in a row. Each one has a stem and a circle.
quests.question: b d p q
quests.hint: Ask yourself two questions for each: does the stem go up or down, and is the circle on the left or the right?
quests.explanation: These four letters are the same shape flipped or turned. Two quick questions, stem direction and circle side, solve them all.
quests.funFact: The shapes b, d, p and q can all be turned into each other by flipping or turning the letter around.

quests.instruction: Write p and q one after the other. Both have a stem that goes below the baseline.
quests.question: p q
quests.hint: p: stem first, circle on the right. q: circle first, stem on the right. Both stems go below the line.
quests.explanation: p and q are mirror images, so the order of strokes is the best clue: p starts with the stem, q starts with the circle.
quests.funFact: In metal printing, each letter was cast backwards so that it printed the right way round.

quests.instruction: Write q, p, p in that order. Make the descenders the same length.
quests.question: q p p
quests.hint: Write q with a circle first, then two p's with the stem first. Tails should be the same length.
quests.explanation: Repeating a letter after its twin builds the habit of choosing the right start every time.
quests.funFact: The saying 'mind your p's and q's' means to be careful about your manners.

quests.instruction: Write q, d, p, b in a row. Think about how each one is built.
quests.question: q d p b
quests.hint: q: circle then stem down. d: circle then stem up. p: stem then circle. b: stem then circle.
quests.explanation: Four letters again, now in a different order. If it helps, think about turning one around to get another.
quests.funFact: If you turn the letter b halfway around, upside down, it becomes q.

quests.instruction: Write n and u. Turn the page upside down: one looks like the other.
quests.question: n u
quests.hint: n has an arch and u has a cup. Make both exactly the same height and width.
quests.explanation: n and u are upside-down versions of each other. Their size and shape should match.
quests.funFact: A word that reads the same upside down is called an ambigram; SWIMS is one.

quests.instruction: Write m and w. They are upside-down twins too.
quests.question: m w
quests.hint: m has two arches, w has two valleys. Make the arches and valleys the same size.
quests.explanation: m and w are upside-down shapes of each other. Practise one to improve the other.
quests.funFact: If you turn the word 'mom' upside down, it reads 'wow'.

quests.instruction: Write n, m, u and w in a row. Keep the spaces equal.
quests.question: n m u w
quests.hint: n and m have arches, u and w have cups. Say 'arch, arch, cup, cup' as you write them.
quests.explanation: Four letters from two families. Writing them together lets you see how they relate.
quests.funFact: A palindrome is a word that reads the same backwards, such as 'level'.

quests.instruction: Write the first three letters, a, b and c, in lowercase.
quests.question: a b c
quests.hint: a: circle then short stem. b: tall stem then bump. c: open curve. Check each height.
quests.explanation: The first three letters use three different formation types: circle with stem, stem with bump, open curve.
quests.funFact: 'ABC' is used to mean the basics of anything, as in 'the ABC of cooking'.

quests.instruction: Write d, e, f and g in lowercase, in order.
quests.question: d e f g
quests.hint: d: circle and tall stem. e: line and curve. f: curve, stem and bar. g: circle and hook below.
quests.explanation: Four letters with ascenders, descenders and small parts, all in one row. Remember each height.
quests.funFact: In music, the notes are named with the letters A to G.

quests.instruction: Write a to g in order, all seven lowercase letters.
quests.question: a b c d e f g
quests.correctAnswer: a b c d e f g
quests.hint: Plan the space for seven letters. Keep gaps equal and check heights as you go.
quests.explanation: Seven different shapes in a row mean seven decisions. Take them one at a time.
quests.funFact: In computing, the letters A to F are used as digits for numbers ten to fifteen in a system called hexadecimal.

quests.instruction: Write h, i and j in lowercase. Remember the dots on the last two.
quests.question: h i j
quests.hint: Write all of h first, then i and its dot, and j and its dot. Check that both dots are above their stems.
quests.explanation: The letters i and j are the only two letters in English that have a dot.
quests.funFact: Some speakers, mostly in Ireland, say the name of the letter h as 'haitch'.

quests.instruction: Write k, l, m and n in lowercase, in order.
quests.question: k l m n
quests.hint: k has slants, l is a tall stem, m has two arches, n has one. Take care of the heights.
quests.explanation: Letters that share stems and arches need careful spacing, so they don't merge.
quests.funFact: In the Greek alphabet, kappa, lambda, mu and nu come one after another, and they match our k, l, m and n.

quests.instruction: Write h to n in order, all seven lowercase letters.
quests.question: h i j k l m n
quests.correctAnswer: h i j k l m n
quests.hint: Plan the space for seven letters before you start. Keep the tall letters at the same height.
quests.explanation: A longer row of letters shows whether your size and spacing stay steady.
quests.funFact: The English alphabet is also called the Roman alphabet or the Latin alphabet.

quests.instruction: Write o, p and q in lowercase. Two of them have tails.
quests.question: o p q
quests.hint: o is a circle, p has a stem going down on its left, q has a stem going down on its right.
quests.explanation: These three share a circle shape. Tails and stems tell them apart.
quests.funFact: The Greek letter rho looks like our P but sounds like our R.

quests.instruction: Write r, s and t in lowercase, in order.
quests.question: r s t
quests.hint: r is a stem and half arch, s is a smooth double curve, t is a stem with a cross.
quests.explanation: Three small letters of different heights. Notice that t is a little taller than r and s.
quests.funFact: The letters r, s and t are among the most common consonants in English.

quests.instruction: Write o to t in order, six lowercase letters.
quests.question: o p q r s t
quests.correctAnswer: o p q r s t
quests.hint: Keep all the circles the same size. Descenders on p and q should be the same length.
quests.explanation: Six lowercase letters including two descenders make this a challenge for spacing and size.
quests.funFact: Typed letters on old typewriters struck an inked ribbon.

quests.instruction: Write u, v and w in lowercase, in order.
quests.question: u v w
quests.hint: u has a curve and a stem, v is a point, w is two points. Keep all three the same height.
quests.explanation: Three letters with different bottoms: a curve, a point, and two points.
quests.funFact: In Spanish, the letter w is used only in words borrowed from other languages.

quests.instruction: Write x, y and z in lowercase, in order.
quests.question: x y z
quests.hint: x is a cross, y has a tail, z has three strokes. Make y's tail go below the baseline.
quests.explanation: The final three letters use slanted strokes. Checking angles is key.
quests.funFact: The phrase 'from A to Z' means 'everything'.

quests.instruction: Write u to z in order, six lowercase letters.
quests.question: u v w x y z
quests.correctAnswer: u v w x y z
quests.hint: Slants and curves in a row: take care with each corner. Keep the letters between the middle line and baseline, except y.
quests.explanation: You have now written the whole alphabet in lowercase in small chunks.
quests.funFact: The last letter of the Greek alphabet is omega, so 'alpha and omega' means beginning and end.

quests.instruction: From memory, write the first half of the lowercase alphabet: a to m.
quests.question: a b c d e f g h i j k l m
quests.correctAnswer: a b c d e f g h i j k l m
quests.hint: Recite the letters quietly as you write. Make all the small letters the same height.
quests.explanation: Writing the alphabet from memory shows which letters your hand knows well.
quests.funFact: The Phoenician alphabet had 22 letters, and all of them were consonants.

quests.instruction: From memory, write the second half of the lowercase alphabet: n to z.
quests.question: n o p q r s t u v w x y z
quests.correctAnswer: n o p q r s t u v w x y z
quests.hint: Think of the groups: round letters, straight letters, slanted letters. Keep your tails the same length.
quests.explanation: Thirteen letters in a row. If one looks too big, make the next one match the others.
quests.funFact: The Arabic alphabet has 28 letters.

quests.instruction: Write the letters at both ends of the alphabet, taking turns: a, z, b, y, c, x.
quests.question: a z b y c x
quests.correctAnswer: a z b y c x
quests.hint: Think: the first letter, the last letter, the second, the second last, and so on.
quests.explanation: Jumping between the start and end of the alphabet makes you recall letters out of order.
quests.funFact: The Russian alphabet has 33 letters.

quests.instruction: Write four i's in a row. Keep all the stems the same height and slant.
quests.question: i i i i
quests.hint: Start each stem at the middle line, pull down to the baseline, and put the dot above it. Check that all the stems are parallel.
quests.explanation: Parallel stems are the secret of neat writing. If one leans differently, it stands out.
quests.funFact: In Turkish, there is a dotted i and a dotless ı, and they are different letters.

quests.instruction: Write four n's in a row. Keep the arches equal.
quests.question: n n n n
quests.hint: Use the same arch each time. Start each stem at the middle line and end on the baseline.
quests.explanation: Repeating the same letter reveals how even your arches are. Match each one to the first.
quests.funFact: In the 1800s, many schools taught a style of handwriting called Spencerian script.

quests.instruction: Write four e's in a row. Keep the middle bars level.
quests.question: e e e e
quests.hint: Draw the bar to the right first, then curve. The bars should line up in a row.
quests.explanation: Level bars on e show good control of horizontal lines.
quests.funFact: Many languages add marks to e, like the accent in 'café'.

quests.instruction: From memory, write the top row of a keyboard in lowercase: q, w, e, r, t, y, u, i, o, p.
quests.question: q w e r t y u i o p
quests.correctAnswer: q w e r t y u i o p
quests.hint: Ten letters is a long row. Say them in your head one by one and check the spacing as you go.
quests.explanation: Writing letters out of alphabetical order means you can't rely on a pattern. It tests your memory of every shape.
quests.funFact: People who type with all ten fingers without looking are called touch typists.

quests.instruction: Write the middle row of a keyboard in lowercase: a, s, d, f, g, h, j, k, l.
quests.question: a s d f g h j k l
quests.correctAnswer: a s d f g h j k l
quests.hint: Nine letters this time. Keep your tall letters, d, f, h, k, l, equal in height, and let g and j drop below.
quests.explanation: The middle row has tall, short and tail letters all in one row. Handling all three shows great control.
quests.funFact: The F and J keys on most keyboards have small bumps so fingers can find them without looking.

quests.instruction: Write the bottom row of a keyboard in lowercase: z, x, c, v, b, n, m.
quests.question: z x c v b n m
quests.correctAnswer: z x c v b n m
quests.hint: Seven letters. Only b is tall. Keep the others between the middle line and the baseline.
quests.explanation: You have written every lowercase letter in a different order. That is real mastery.
quests.funFact: On a computer, pressing the Control key with C copies and with V pastes.
